headline: Solar incentives in Kansas in 2026
summary: With federal 25D unavailable for typical 2026 homeowner completes, Kansas solar economics lean on utility export rules, any state production/rebate programs, tax treatment, and system cost. Confirm primary sources — this page is a planning overview.
net_metering_or_billing_overview: Export compensation is utility- and state-specific. Start with your utility guide, then check the state energy office / DSIRE-style directories against primary .gov pages.
property_tax_sales_tax_notes: Check whether the state offers sales or property tax exemptions for residential solar.
hoa_solar_access_law: Some states limit HOA bans on solar. Confirm current statute before assuming protection.

sections.heading: Federal credit reality in 2026
sections.body: Section 25D generally does not apply to expenditures made after Dec 31, 2025. Do not model a 30% federal rebate for a new cash/loan install unless your tax advisor says otherwise.

sections.heading: Where to verify Kansas programs
sections.body: Use the official state energy office, utility rebate portals, and interconnection tariffs. Aggregator blogs go stale quickly after OBBBA.

faqs.question: Is solar worth it in Kansas without the federal tax credit?
faqs.answer: It depends on rates, export rules, state incentives, and installed $/W. Model your address and compare quotes with labeled assumptions.
